maya: PRD intake — observability for model rollouts
maya: Problem statement: customers and SREs lack reliable per-rollout metrics (quality/regression, latency, cost) to safely run canary and A/B rollouts. Current logs + per-request traces are noisy and don't map to rollout versions.
maya: Goals: 1) expose per-rollout time-series (quality delta, p95/p99 latency, token cost) + per-tenant isolation where applicable, 2) provide alerting and canary pass/fail rules, 3) lightweight dashboard template + API for programmatic checks.
maya: Non-goals: we will not ship deep-label-based evaluation (manual human eval) in phase 1, not building a full retraining pipeline.
maya: Success metrics: 1) 90% of internal rollout failures detected by automated canary checks within 10m, 2) reduce manual rollback ops by 40% for first customers, 3) FortuneApp pilot adoption within 6 weeks.
maya: Acceptance criteria (high level): - API that accepts rollout_id and returns metrics windowed by version - Canary config schema + evaluator running on platform - Dashboard + raw metric export for tenants - Docs + quickstart + e2e test harness
maya: Edge cases to call out: traffic skew (tiny tenants), cold-starts for new model versions, cross-tenant noisy neighbors, missing labels for quality metrics.

arik: Q — for per-tenant isolation do we need separate ingestion pipelines (Kafka/topic) or can we tag and filter in existing pipeline?
samir: I'd prefer tagging to start, but tagging + separate workspace metrics for Dedicated customers. tagging keeps latency low.
dana: FWIW FortuneApp requires strict data isolation for rollout metrics; they'd prefer a dedicated metrics workspace or at least per-tenant encryption keys.
sean: Engineering reality: building a dedicated pipeline and retention policy is ~3 weeks infra work + 1 week testing. Tagging + RBAC filters is 1 week. We should phase.
maya: Proposed phased scope:
- Phase 1 (hosted): tagging, canary evaluator running against aggregated metrics, dashboard template, API for rollouts.
- Phase 2 (dedicated customers): dedicated ingestion workspace, per-tenant retention and encryption options, SLA for metric latency.

arik: Example canary config we expect from customers? can we standardize?
maya: here's a minimal schema we can start with:
```json
{
  "rollout_id": "r-12345",
  "baseline_version": "v1.2",
  "candidate_version": "v1.3",
  "metrics": [
    {"name": "p99_latency_ms", "threshold_pct": 150, "direction": "lower"},
    {"name": "safety_regression", "threshold_abs": 0.02, "direction": "lower"}
  ],
  "window": "5m",
  "aggregation": "p95,p99,mean"
}
```

prd-bot: RFC draft created: /docs/rfcs/1769001234-model-rollout-observability.md (assigned to maya)

maya: Next steps: assign owners for infra, evaluator, docs; flesh out final ACs and schedule RFC review. Suggest Wed 10am review slot.
arik: I can own infra (ingestion/tagging + canary infra).
samir: I'll own dashboards and SLI definitions.
dana: I'll own customer coordination for FortuneApp and confirm isolation needs.
sean: I'll scope e2e test harness and the alerting runbooks.
maya: Great — will update the RFC and add acceptance criteria including test cases and a small synthetic regression test. Will also add rollback playbook notes.
dana: Customer asks: please include cost attribution per rollout for billing stakeholders — they want per-rollout token cost exported.
maya: noted, add to ACs for phase 1 (estimate accuracy +/-10%).
arik: one more edge case: model chain requests that fan-out to multiple models — we need to surface per-submodel metrics or at least attribution heuristics.
samir: agreed, add a "span" tag for downstream model calls; we can approximate cost attribution.
maya: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll post the RFC link and agenda after this thread.
